original_question: Let g be a primitive cusp form of weight k for Gamma_0(N), normalized so that its first Fourier coefficient is 1 and written as g(z) = sum_{n>=0} lambda_g(n) n^((k-1)/2) e(nz). Let F(x,y) be a smooth weight function supported on (X/4, 4X] x [Y/4, 4Y], satisfying the derivative bounds stated in the paper, and define the shifted convolution sum D_g(ell_1, ell_2; h) = sum_{ell_1 m +/- ell_2 n = h} lambda_g(n) lambda_g(m) F(ell_1 m, ell_2 n) for coprime ell_1 and ell_2. Determine how the explicit constant in the known asymptotic upper bounds depends on k and N, and in the full modular-group case prove a weight-uniform asymptotic upper bound useful for Rankin-Selberg moment problems with large weights.
target_in_paper: Problem (30) in the subsection "ADDITIVE DIVISOR SUMS/SHIFTED CONVOLUTION SUMS" of the paper’s Problems section; for arXiv:2405.17800, this is the exact numbered open problem your draft is paraphrasing. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17800))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures almost all of the paper’s intended setup: the primitive cusp form g of weight k for Γ0(N), the arithmetic normalization a_g(1)=1, the Fourier expansion g(z)=∑_{n≥0} λ_g(n)n^((k-1)/2)e(nz), the smooth weight F supported on (X/4,4X]×[Y/4,4Y], the shifted convolution sum D_g(ℓ1,ℓ2;h), the coprimality of ℓ1 and ℓ2, and the two actual goals stated in the paper—making the constant depend explicitly on k and N, and proving a weight-uniform upper bound in the full modular-group case for Rankin-Selberg moment applications. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
missing_details: The paper does not contain Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; for this arXiv ID the relevant target is the numbered open Problem (30). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17800))
The hypotheses X,Y,P≥1 should be stated explicitly. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

To make the question stand-alone, the derivative condition on F should be written explicitly as x^i y^j(∂_x^i∂_y^jF)(x,y) ≪ P^(i+j) for all i,j≥0, rather than referring back to the paper. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

The question should name the specific prior results being sharpened: Harcos proved an asymptotic upper bound for D_g(ℓ1,ℓ2;h), and Blomer-Harcos proved an averaged asymptotic bound, with constants depending on g. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2405.17800v1))
Full modular group should be identified explicitly as the special case N=1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2405.17800v1))

The shift h and the coprime integers ℓ1,ℓ2 should be quantified explicitly; the paper leaves them as general parameters, so the refined question should not silently fix ranges that the paper does not fix. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

To remain paper-faithful, the target in the N=1 case should be an asymptotic upper bound uniform in the weight aspect, not a stronger claim such as a full asymptotic formula or level-uniformity. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2405.17800v1))

The paper does not prescribe the final shape of the bound, so the refined question should not add extra exponents, ranges, or secondary hypotheses not present in Problem (30). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2405.17800v1))
refined_question: Let g be a primitive holomorphic cusp form of weight k for Γ0(N), arithmetically normalized by a_g(1)=1 and written as g(z)=∑_{n≥0} λ_g(n)n^((k-1)/2)e(nz). Let X,Y,P≥1, and let F:(0,∞)^2→ℂ be a smooth function supported on (X/4,4X]×[Y/4,4Y] such that x^i y^j(∂_x^i∂_y^jF)(x,y) ≪ P^(i+j) for all i,j≥0. For coprime integers ℓ1,ℓ2 and an integer shift h, define D_g(ℓ1,ℓ2;h)=∑_{ℓ1m±ℓ2n=h} λ_g(n)λ_g(m)F(ℓ1m,ℓ2n). Determine explicitly how the constants in Harcos’s asymptotic upper bound for D_g(ℓ1,ℓ2;h) and in the Blomer-Harcos averaged bound depend on the weight k and level N of g; moreover, in the full modular-group case N=1, prove an asymptotic upper bound for D_g(ℓ1,ℓ2;h) that is uniform in the weight aspect k and is suitable for applications to moment problems for Rankin-Selberg L-functions attached to primitive forms of large weight. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2405.17800v1))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper: arXiv:2405.17800 is a problem list on moments of L-functions and related topics, and Problem (30) is stated directly as an open problem about the shifted convolution sum D_g(ℓ1,ℓ2;h). Your draft is already very close, but the paper-faithful sharpening is to identify Harcos and Blomer-Harcos as the specific prior bounds under discussion, to spell out the derivative hypotheses and ambient parameters explicitly, and to keep the N=1 objective at exactly the level stated in the paper—an asymptotic upper bound uniform in the weight aspect for applications to Rankin-Selberg moment problems. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
